title: how much of E527's whole published arm population closes once E536's interpreter has the caller module's own functions and one hop of free-name binding inside the argument expression
population_source: e548_extended_resolver.py::population() -- every arm in UNDECIDABLEARM-2026-11-08.json, in published order
method_limits: the resolver is E536's interpreter with two switches: the caller module's own top-level functions in its _fn_map, and one hop of binding for the free names inside the argument expression; all four combinations are published per arm
an arm whose guard names no parameter is not moved by any argument resolver and is counted as such rather than folded into the closed fraction
one_hop_out is published only for an arm whose argument is the caller's own parameter, and only over that caller's call sites in the same module
an item store between a binding and the site is not replayed (E544's subject); a folding call site makes the arm actionable, it does not make it closed here

the arms E527 itself declared settled are re-checked under this resolver and published as parent_settlement_reproduced: this resolver refuses to read module state, so a settlement that rests on a module-level constant is expected to come back open
nothing in this repository is executed and no source is rewritten
a fixture corpus is not a repository: the selftest proves the switches behave as named, the face is the repository's own reading
